title: Rex and the Puddle with a Road
synopsis: Rex follows a tiny roadside stream with his eyes while Jack compares wet grass and pavement and discovers where the water can go.
continuity_state: Before: The overnight rain has ended. The park rain gauge still holds water at its third mark, and a shallow puddle is visible outside Pine Park near the road. After: The friends identify a gently sloping paved curb west of the park gate and an existing grated roadside storm inlet farther downhill. Some rain has soaked into park soil; some flows across the road surface and along the curb. No water is carried, poured into, or blocked at the drain by the children.

related_resources.reason: Supports one narrowly linked factual description, not listener outcome claims.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Some rain soaked into the grassy ground, but water on the road had nowhere to soak through.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Rain can infiltrate porous ground but runs off hard, relatively impervious road surfaces.
